column2: Look down, friend. An iron spear lies on the ground, five paces south-south-west of me, and anyone may pick it up. Take it before the goats find it interesting. Ha.
This is the yard, friend. Every job comes past me here. The goats and the chickens keep the far side, about ten paces west-north-west. Is that not so, my fine ones?
Here a debt is paid in work. An arbitrator turns the loss into months. We count them in nushmeekos, the thankless ones. Work them all and it is over.
An owing can be sold on, friend. Whoever is owed the months may sell them to a person who needs hands. The worker goes with them, sacks and all.
I am Lifts-The-Sacks. I load the rice and do the heavy work others will not do. My uncle ran up a debt. I am working off the months. Do not pity me, friend. I am strong. The flood is coming. Ha.
Reads-The-Shallows, the boat captain, waits about ten paces north-north-west of here. Go and speak to the captain, friend. I like that one. They thank me.
